Captain of Fifty
KAP-tin uv FIF-tee
noun
From captain (Old French capitain, from Latin caput, head) and fifty. It renders the Hebrew sar 'hāmishshīm — a junior officer over a company of fifty men, the lowest of the graded commands Jethro set up in Exodus 18.

Biblical Definition

The captain of fifty is a junior officer — the lowest rung of the graded command Jethro counselled Moses to appoint, “rulers of thousands, and rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens” (Exo 18:21). He is a real rank in Israel's civil and military order, and Isaiah lists him among the props God threatens to pull out from under Judah: “The captain of fifty, and the honourable man, and the counsellor” (Isa 3:3). But he is remembered for one narrative. Ahaziah, injured and enquiring of Baalzebub, sends soldiers to fetch Elijah down from his hill. The first comes with a summons in his mouth: “Thou man of God, the king hath said, Come down” (2Ki 1:9) — and fire falls. The second comes the same way, and fire falls again. Then comes the third, and everything changes, not in the rank but in the man: “the third captain of fifty went up, and came and fell on his knees before Elijah, and besought him, and said unto him, O man of God, I pray thee, let my life, and the life of these fifty thy servants, be precious in thy sight” (2Ki 1:13). He had seen what happened to the two before him, and he drew the right conclusion (2Ki 1:14). Here is the whole difference between summoning God and beseeching Him. The two who commanded the prophet died; the one who begged lived, and his fifty with him.

Webster 1828 Definition

A junior officer set over a company of fifty men; the lowest of Israel's graded commands.

expand to see more

CAPTAIN OF FIFTY, an officer commanding a company of fifty men.

Hebrew sar 'hāmishshīm; the least of the ranks of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens (Exo 18:21).

A standing rank in Israel's civil and military order, and in the king's guard.

Isaiah names him among the stays of the state that God threatens to remove (Isa 3:3).

Three such captains were sent to Elijah; two were consumed and the third was spared (2Ki 1).

Key Scripture

2Ki 1:9 — "Then the king sent unto him a captain of fifty with his fifty. And he went up to him: and, behold, he sat on the top of an hill. And he spake unto him, Thou man of God, the king hath said, Come down."

2Ki 1:13 — "And he sent again a captain of the third fifty with his fifty. And the third captain of fifty went up, and came and fell on his knees before Elijah, and besought him, and said unto him, O man of God, I pray thee, let my life, and the life of these fifty thy servants, be precious in thy sight."

2Ki 1:14 — "Behold, there came fire down from heaven, and burnt up the two captains of the former fifties with their fifties: therefore let my life now be precious in thy sight."

Isa 3:3 — "The captain of fifty, and the honourable man, and the counsellor, and the cunning artificer, and the eloquent orator."

Modern Corruption

A minor rank with a major lesson; the corruption is the modern habit of approaching God as a superior officer issues an order.

expand to see more

Ahaziah's captains carry the king's tone into the presence of the LORD's prophet, and the tone is the sin. “The king hath said, Come down” — a summons, a schedule, an expectation of compliance. Whole streams of modern religion have institutionalised exactly that posture: the word of faith teacher who instructs the believer to decree and declare, to command his healing, to call things into being as though the creature had the Creator's prerogative; the practical deism of the man who prays as one files a requisition and is offended when it is not filled. The name of God has been made a lever. Fire from heaven is the biblical estimate of that error, and it fell twice before the lesson took.

The third captain is the corrective, and he is not a better man — he is a wiser one. He climbs the same hill on the same errand under the same king, but he comes on his knees and asks that his life be precious in the prophet's sight, and he goes down alive with his fifty behind him. That is how sinners come to God: not summoning but beseeching, not decreeing but pleading, casting themselves on a mercy they cannot compel. “God be merciful to me a sinner” is the third captain's prayer in the temple, and the LORD who would not be commanded off His hill has never yet refused a man who came up it on his knees.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Captain of fifty = a junior officer over fifty men; Hebrew sar 'hāmishshīm.

expand to see more

Captain of fifty — Latin caput, head; the head of a company of fifty.

The lowest of Jethro's four grades: thousands, hundreds, fifties, tens (Exo 18:21).

A distinct rank from the captain of the host, who commanded an entire army.

Isaiah lists him among the stays God will take away from Judah (Isa 3:3).

Two such captains commanded Elijah and were consumed; the third besought him and lived.

Usage

"The king hath said, Come down — and fire came down instead."

"Two captains summoned the prophet and died; the third besought him and lived."

"The rank never changed; the knees did."
